Preconditions: You have the HTTPS admin link, shop email, and password.
Use case: Shop staff can open the admin website and sign in.
What to do: 1. Open the admin website. 2. Enter the shop email and password. 3. Sign in.
What you should see: You land on the Dashboard. Menu shows Dashboard, Orders, Reports, Audit log, Products, Customers, Profile, Announcements, Shop status, Preferences. Announcements has Poster and Inbox & phone tabs (no separate Notifications menu). Version and Sign out are at the bottom of the menu.

Preconditions: A customer Google or email account (not shop admin).
Use case: A customer login cannot be used as shop admin.
What to do: Try to sign in with a non-admin account or a wrong password.
What you should see: You see a clear Not authorized (or sign-in failed) message. You do not see orders, customers, or sales.

Preconditions: Customer app installed. Not signed in.
Use case: A visitor can look at products before signing in.
What to do: On the first screen confirm Continue with Google and Continue with Email (no Sign in with Mobile Number). Tap Skip. Browse Home.
What you should see: Products are visible. Placing an order, opening Orders, Notifications, or saving an address asks you to sign in.

Preconditions: Preview or Play APK (not a Metro development client). Google account on the phone.
Use case: A customer signs in with Google.
What to do: 1. Tap Continue with Google. 2. Choose the Google account on the phone. 3. Allow Farm2Flavour if asked.
What you should see: You reach Home signed in. Account shows the Google name or email. The phone must not open a Google website that says continue to supabase.co.

Preconditions: Email you can open on this phone. No custom SMTP required.
Use case: A customer signs in with the email link.
What to do: 1. Tap Continue with Email. 2. Enter the email. 3. Tap Send confirmation email. 4. Open mail from Supabase Auth. 5. Tap Sign in on this phone and return to the app.
What you should see: The Check your email screen explains the Supabase Auth mail. After the link you are on Home. There is no 6-digit box for email.

Preconditions: You are on the Check your email screen.
Use case: If the email is late, the customer can ask again.
What to do: Wait if the button counts down, then tap Resend email.
What you should see: A new mail arrives. If you tap too fast, the app may ask you to wait about a minute.

Preconditions: Delivery APK. Same email and password as the admin website.
Use case: A driver signs in with the shop admin login.
What to do: Open the delivery app. Enter the admin email and password (not a customer Google or email link).
What you should see: Today’s deliveries opens.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. Some orders exist for today (India time).
Use case: The shop can see today’s work at a glance.
What to do: Look at Orders today, Sales today, Delivered today, and Outstanding.
What you should see: Numbers match orders you know for today. If money is still owed, Outstanding is highlighted. Tap Outstanding to open Reports.

Preconditions: At least one order is still Placed.
Use case: The shop is reminded when new orders are waiting.
What to do: Look at the top of the Dashboard. Tap the waiting banner if shown.
What you should see: A banner says how many orders wait to be confirmed. Tap opens Orders on the Placed tab.

Preconditions: Phone browser. Admin login.
Use case: Staff can use the admin site on a phone.
What to do: Open Menu. Open Dashboard, Orders, and Reports.
What you should see: Lists show as cards you can tap. You can open an order without sideways scrolling.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: The shop can add a product customers can buy.
What to do: 1. Open Products. 2. Add product. 3. Photo, name, selling type Qty, price. 4. Save.
What you should see: The product is Active and Available. The customer app shows it with Add.

Preconditions: At least two products; one already used on an order.
Use case: The shop can hide a product or mark it not ready.
What to do: Set one product Inactive. Set another Coming soon. Try to delete a product that was already ordered.
What you should see: Inactive disappears from the customer app. Coming soon is dimmed with no Add (Notify me may show). Ordered products cannot be deleted; use Inactive.

Preconditions: Admin on a laptop. CSV template available.
Use case: The shop can load many products from a spreadsheet.
What to do: 1. Products → Export template. 2. Fill a few rows. 3. Import CSV.
What you should see: You see how many imported and skipped. Failed rows have an error log. At most 250 products per file.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: Staff can save a Kg product with price per Kg and weight options.
What to do: Selling type Kg. Price per Kg 100. Enable options such as 250g and 500g. Optional min/max. Save.
What you should see: Customer app shows From ₹ / Kg and those weight chips. There is no free weight text box.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: Staff can save independent pack prices.
What to do: Selling type Fixed pack. Add 100g at ₹50 and 250g at ₹125. Deactivate 100g. Save.
What you should see: Customer app shows only 250g. Prices are not calculated from per-Kg.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: Staff can save a quantity product with a unit price.
What to do: Selling type Qty. Price 60. Save.
What you should see: Customer listing shows ₹60. There is no Bottle/Piece unit picker.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: Staff can save a Liter product with volume options.
What to do: Selling type Liter. Price per Liter 80. Enable 500ml and 1 L. Save.
What you should see: Customer app shows ₹80 / L and those volume chips. Line total is per L × volume × qty.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. At least one product.
Use case: The shop can group products (for example Sweets, Oils).
What to do: 1. Products → Categories. 2. Turn categories on. 3. Add a category with name and picture. 4. Put a product in it.
What you should see: On customer Home, chips sit under search (All, then your categories). Tapping a chip filters Home and search.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: The shop can add a customer who ordered by phone.
What to do: Customers → Add customer. Name and 10-digit mobile. Save. Try the same mobile again.
What you should see: Saved as Phone / Offline. Second time: mobile already exists and offers to open that customer.

Preconditions: An admin customer record exists.
Use case: The shop can keep up to three addresses and delivery notes.
What to do: Open a customer. Add or edit addresses and instructions. Set a default. Try a fourth address.
What you should see: At most 3 addresses. Instructions are visible to the shop. Default is used next time.

Preconditions: One customer with orders, one with none.
Use case: The shop cannot erase a customer who already has orders.
What to do: Try Delete on both customers.
What you should see: With orders: cannot delete. With no orders: can delete.

Preconditions: Customer signed in. Shop has at least one poster and categories.
Use case: Home shows greeting, search, then posters under categories.
What to do: Open Home in the morning or afternoon. Scroll the product list. Pull the list so the poster moves.
What you should see: A greeting such as Good afternoon shows. Search stays at the top. Posters sit under category chips and scroll away with the list. Search is not above the address row.

Preconditions: Customer app on a phone.
Use case: The customer app does not offer voice ordering or the microphone.
What to do: Look at Home. Then check this app’s permissions in phone Settings.
What you should see: No Order by Voice card. The app does not ask for the microphone. Notifications may still be listed.

Preconditions: Customer signed in. Products and optional categories exist.
Use case: A customer finds a product and adds it.
What to do: Tap Search products and type part of a name. If chips exist, tap one while search is open. Tap back. Then Add and use + and −.
What you should see: Search fills the screen; posters hide. Categories stay under search and still filter. Back returns to Home and shows posters. A View cart bar shows the count.

Preconditions: A product is Coming soon.
Use case: A product that is not ready cannot be bought.
What to do: Find the Coming soon product on Home or search.
What you should see: It looks dimmed. No Add (Notify me may show). It cannot go in the cart.

Preconditions: Customer has at least one delivered or past order with items. Cancelled-only history is not enough.
Use case: A returning customer can reorder usual items.
What to do: Open the Order again tab.
What you should see: You see products from recent orders (cancelled orders ignored). You can search and add them.

Preconditions: Customer signed in. Several available products.
Use case: The cart has sensible limits.
What to do: Try more than 15 different products, or more than 10 of one product. Use Clear cart.
What you should see: The app explains the limit in plain words. Clear cart asks to confirm, then empties the cart.

Preconditions: At least one item in the cart.
Use case: A customer can remove one item from the cart.
What to do: Swipe an item left and tap the bin, or reduce quantity below 1.
What you should see: That item leaves the cart. The total updates.

Preconditions: Item is in the cart. Shop can mark it Coming soon.
Use case: The customer cannot place an order if an item became Coming soon.
What to do: Add a product. Shop marks it Coming soon. Try Place order.
What you should see: The app asks you to remove that item before you can place the order.

Preconditions: A Kg product with 500g option. Customer signed in.
Use case: Customer picks an admin-set Kg weight option and a quantity.
What to do: Open the Kg product. Confirm there is no weight text box. Tap 500g, raise quantity to 2, Add to cart.
What you should see: Cart shows 2 × 500g. Line total is 2 × (per Kg × 0.5). Quantity is limited to 1–10.

Preconditions: A fixed-pack product with 250g.
Use case: Customer can pick a pack and a pack count.
What to do: Choose 250g. Set quantity 2. Add to cart.
What you should see: Cart shows 2 × 250g and line total 2 × pack price.

Preconditions: A Qty product.
Use case: Customer can order whole-number quantity only.
What to do: Increase to 3. Confirm there is no decimal qty. Place if you want.
What you should see: Cart shows Product × 3. Line total is 3 × unit price.

Preconditions: Kg product whose weight options are all deactivated.
Use case: A Kg product with no active weight options cannot be ordered.
What to do: Open it in the customer app.
What you should see: The product page says no weight options are available. Add is not possible.

Preconditions: A Liter product with 500ml option.
Use case: Customer picks an admin-set Liter volume option and a quantity.
What to do: Open the Liter product. No volume text box. Tap 500ml, quantity 2, Add.
What you should see: Cart shows 2 × 500ml. Line total is 2 × (per L × 0.5). Quantity 1–10.

Preconditions: Admin Preferences has a min order amount (for example ₹200). Cart total is below that.
Use case: Checkout is blocked until the cart meets the shop minimum.
What to do: Add items so the total is under the minimum. Try Place order. Then add enough to pass.
What you should see: The app explains the minimum and blocks Place order. After the total meets the minimum, Place order works.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. Sellable products exist.
Use case: The shop can type a phone or walk-in order.
What to do: Orders → Create order. Pick or add customer and address. Search products, add a sellable item. Choose Cash, UPI, or Not yet. Create order.
What you should see: Coming soon and Inactive names appear in search groups and cannot be added. Payment fills the whole button. Order is Phone / Offline with prices from the product list.

Preconditions: Several orders exist.
Use case: The shop can find orders and download a list.
What to do: Use status tabs. Search by number, name, or phone. Date filter. Export.
What you should see: List matches filters. Export is a spreadsheet. Next page when more than 25.

Preconditions: A customer order is Placed. Customer phone has alerts on (optional).
Use case: The shop confirms a new customer order.
What to do: Open the Placed order. Tap Confirm order and confirm.
What you should see: Status is Confirmed. Customer app shows Confirmed. Phone and in-app Notifications get an orders row if alerts/inbox are on.

Preconditions: Order is Placed or Confirmed.
Use case: The shop can change items before the order goes out.
What to do: Modify order. Add, remove, or change quantities. Review and update. Optional note.
What you should see: Customer sees Shop modified until View changes. The customer’s 5-change limit is not used up.

Preconditions: Order is Confirmed.
Use case: The shop sends the order out and marks it delivered.
What to do: Mark out for delivery, then Mark as delivered. Choose Cash, UPI, or Not yet.
What you should see: Each step has date and time. Customer sees the same steps. Not yet leaves it outstanding.

Preconditions: Order status was set by mistake.
Use case: The shop can undo a wrong status click.
What to do: … menu → Fix a status mistake. Pick the correct status and save.
What you should see: Order and customer app show the corrected status.

Preconditions: An open or unpaid order the shop needs to cancel.
Use case: The shop can cancel an order and must say why.
What to do: … → Cancel order. Pick a reason or Other with a short note. Confirm.
What you should see: Order is Cancelled. Customer sees that reason. If it was paid, Refund pending.

Preconditions: Kg product with 250g option.
Use case: Staff can add a Kg line to a phone order using an option and quantity.
What to do: New order. Add the Kg product. Choose 250g. Quantity 3. Place.
What you should see: Line shows 3 × 250g with price per Kg × 0.25 × 3. No free weight box.

Preconditions: Customer signed in, address saved, cart meets min order, shop open, online.
Use case: A customer places an order to be paid on delivery.
What to do: Check Deliver to. Tap Place order.
What you should see: Thank-you screen with order number and amount. Your Orders lists it. Pay on delivery is cash or UPI only.

Preconditions: An order is still Placed or Confirmed for an address.
Use case: The same house cannot have two open orders at once.
What to do: Try to start another order to that address.
What you should see: The app explains there is already an active order and offers View / Modify. Another address still works.

Preconditions: Two saved addresses.
Use case: Two addresses can each have their own open order.
What to do: Place one open order on each address.
What you should see: Both show under Your Orders and stay separate.

Preconditions: First order for an address is Out for delivery.
Use case: Once an order is on the way, the customer can order again to that address.
What to do: Start another order for the same address.
What you should see: The screen says an order is on the way and still lets you deliver a new order there.

Preconditions: Order is Placed or Confirmed.
Use case: A customer can change an open order until it is out for delivery.
What to do: Tap Modify. Change items. Update order. Also try Discard and Exit.
What you should see: Order updated successfully. Discard restores. Exit without save if confirmed. Modify is gone after Out for delivery.

Preconditions: Order is Placed or Confirmed.
Use case: A customer can change one order only five times.
What to do: Modify the same order until the app stops you.
What you should see: After 5 updates it says the modify limit is reached. It also says you can still cancel until Out for delivery.

Preconditions: One Placed order and one Confirmed order. Customer signed in.
Use case: A customer can cancel while Placed or Confirmed, and must pick a reason.
What to do: On Placed: Cancel order, pick a reason (for example Ordered by mistake), confirm. On Confirmed: Cancel order, pick Not able to receive order. Then open an Out for delivery order.
What you should see: Placed and Confirmed become Cancelled and show that reason. Out for delivery has no Cancel button.

Preconditions: A cancellable order.
Use case: Cancellation requires a listed reason or Other text.
What to do: Tap Cancel order. Try Other with one letter (button stays off). Then pick Changed my mind or Other with at least three letters.
What you should see: Cancel order stays disabled until a valid reason. After confirm, admin and the order screen show that reason.

Preconditions: Ability to place several small orders (use extra addresses if needed).
Use case: A customer cannot cancel more than three orders in a day.
What to do: Cancel three Placed or Confirmed orders in 24 hours, then try a fourth.
What you should see: Fourth time: cancel limit for today, contact the shop. Shop cancellations do not count.

Preconditions: Shop has modified the customer’s open order.
Use case: The customer can see what the shop changed.
What to do: Open the order. Tap View changes.
What you should see: Added, removed, or quantity changes and old/new total. Shop modified mark goes away after viewing.

Preconditions: Customer is on Modify. Shop can mark Out for delivery.
Use case: If the shop sends the order out while the customer is still editing, the edit is dropped.
What to do: Start Modify. Shop marks Out for delivery before Update order.
What you should see: The app explains the order is on the way (or cancelled/delivered) and unsaved changes were not kept.

Preconditions: At least one order in Your Orders.
Use case: The customer can follow the order step by step.
What to do: Open an order from Your Orders.
What you should see: Order number on the detail screen (not the list). Status, items, address, steps Placed → Confirmed → Out for delivery → Delivered with times.

Preconditions: Placed order for 2 × 500g of a Kg product.
Use case: New order snapshots survive a later product edit.
What to do: Place the order. Then change price per Kg or remove the 500g option in admin. Open the order and a delivery bill if you have one.
What you should see: Order and bill still show 2 × 500g and the original line total.

Preconditions: An old Kg order that used a typed total weight (for example 2.34 Kg).
Use case: Old Kg orders with a typed total weight still display correctly.
What to do: Open that order.
What you should see: The line still reads 2.34 Kg with its original total.

Preconditions: Delivered order that is not paid.
Use case: The shop records cash or UPI after delivery.
What to do: Tap Collect, choose Cash or UPI, mark paid.
What you should see: No longer owed. Reports Outstanding drops by that amount.

Preconditions: A paid order.
Use case: The shop can correct a payment entered by mistake.
What to do: … → Change payment method. Switch Cash and UPI, or Not yet.
What you should see: Payment line matches. Not yet puts the amount back into outstanding.

Preconditions: Cancelled order that was paid. Money returned outside the app.
Use case: The shop records a refund after a paid order is cancelled.
What to do: Tap Mark refunded.
What you should see: Shows Refunded. Not listed as outstanding.

Preconditions: Order is Out for delivery, unpaid. Shop has a UPI QR.
Use case: The customer can pay by UPI when the order is on the way.
What to do: Open the order.
What you should see: Pay by UPI shows that QR. Payment is still collected in person, not inside the app.

Preconditions: Driver marking Delivered.
Use case: The driver records how the customer paid at the door.
What to do: Choose Cash, UPI, or Not yet.
What you should see: Cash or UPI clears the amount. Not yet stays outstanding on Reports. Next screen asks whether to share the bill.

Preconditions: Unpaid delivery. Driver allowed to manage QR.
Use case: The driver can show the shop UPI QR.
What to do: Show the UPI QR. Upload or replace if allowed.
What you should see: Customer app shows the same QR when the order is out for delivery and unpaid.

Preconditions: Signed out of the customer app.
Use case: Notifications asks the customer to sign in.
What to do: Tap the bell on Home, or open Notifications from Account.
What you should see: You are asked to sign in. No message list.

Preconditions: Signed in. Phone notification permission denied.
Use case: Inbox still works when phone alerts are off.
What to do: Deny notifications if asked. Place an order and have the shop Confirm. Open the bell.
What you should see: Bell can show an unread mark and the Confirmed row in the list. No phone banner/sound.

Preconditions: Signed in on a real device. Allow alerts when asked.
Use case: Allowing alerts saves the device for phone pushes.
What to do: Allow notifications. Have the shop Confirm an order.
What you should see: A phone alert arrives for the order. Opening it relates to that order or Notifications.

Preconditions: Signed in. Inbox already opened once while online.
Use case: Without internet, the list can still open; new alerts wait.
What to do: Open Notifications once. Turn on airplane mode. Open the bell again. Have the shop send a message (will not arrive yet). Turn network back on and wait.
What you should see: You can still open the list you already had. After you are online again, new rows can appear.

Preconditions: Signed in. Unread shop or order messages exist.
Use case: Home bell shows unread; reading clears it.
What to do: Look at Home. Open the bell. Tap one unread row. Return to Home. Tap Mark all as read if more remain.
What you should see: Bell shows a count or dot when unread. After read / Mark all as read, the mark is gone.

Preconditions: Several unread rows.
Use case: Mark all as read clears every unread row.
What to do: Open Notifications. Tap Mark all as read.
What you should see: Unread dots disappear. Bell on Home is clear.

Preconditions: Alerts allowed. Order is Placed.
Use case: Confirming an order adds an Orders inbox row and a phone alert.
What to do: Shop taps Confirm. Open Notifications. Filter Orders.
What you should see: A Confirmed row appears under Today (if today). Phone alert if allowed. Filter Orders shows it; Offers does not.

Preconditions: Order is Confirmed. Alerts allowed.
Use case: Out for delivery adds an Orders inbox row and a phone alert.
What to do: Shop marks Out for delivery. Open the bell and the phone shade.
What you should see: Out for delivery message in the list. Phone alert. Tap the row opens that order.

Preconditions: Order is Out for delivery.
Use case: Delivered adds an Orders inbox row.
What to do: Shop or driver marks Delivered. Open Notifications.
What you should see: Delivered message appears. Cancel does not add an extra orders row.

Preconditions: Cancellable order.
Use case: Customer cancel does not create an order-status inbox row.
What to do: Cancel the order with a reason. Open Notifications → Orders.
What you should see: No new “order cancelled” inbox row from that cancel. The order itself shows Cancelled with the reason.

Preconditions: Admin Announcements → Inbox & phone. Customer signed in with alerts on.
Use case: An important update lands in Updates and on the phone.
What to do: Shop sends Type Important update, title and body. Customer opens the bell, then Updates.
What you should see: Row appears in All and Updates, not Offers. Phone alert. Toast on admin: Saved for N customers and Phone alert sent to N devices (or a clear fail line).

Preconditions: Admin Inbox & phone. Customer signed in.
Use case: An offer lands in Offers.
What to do: Shop sends Type Offer. Customer opens Offers.
What you should see: Row appears in All and Offers, not Orders. Phone alert if allowed.

Preconditions: At least one of each: order, offer, update.
Use case: Filters All, Orders, Offers, Updates work. Today sits under the chips.
What to do: Open Notifications. Switch each chip. Look at the gap under the chips.
What you should see: Each chip shows only that type. All shows everything. Today is directly under the chips (no large empty space). Earlier appears only for older days.

Preconditions: Customer who can receive many admin messages (or use several sends).
Use case: The list keeps only the latest 20 messages.
What to do: Send or generate more than 20 inbox rows for that customer. Open the bell.
What you should see: Only 20 rows. Oldest is gone. Unread badge matches what is still in the list.

Preconditions: An unread shop message (no order id).
Use case: Tapping a shop message stays on Notifications.
What to do: Tap the update or offer row.
What you should see: It marks read. You stay on the list (no order screen).

Preconditions: Phone alert for an order status.
Use case: Tapping an order phone alert opens that order.
What to do: From the phone notification, tap the confirmed or out-for-delivery alert.
What you should see: The order screen for that order opens (or Notifications then the order). App does not crash.

Preconditions: Phone alert for an Inbox & phone message.
Use case: Tapping an inbox phone alert opens Notifications.
What to do: Tap the shop message alert on the phone.
What you should see: Notifications list opens. The new message is visible.

Preconditions: Signed out. Coming soon product with Notify me.
Use case: Notify me while signed out asks for sign-in.
What to do: Tap Notify me.
What you should see: Sign-in is required before you are subscribed.

Preconditions: Signed in. Alerts off. Coming soon product.
Use case: Notify me with alerts off prompts for permission.
What to do: Tap Notify me.
What you should see: The app asks to allow notifications or explains they are off. You can still be on the wait list.

Preconditions: Signed in. Notify me already tapped. Alerts on.
Use case: Shop turning Coming soon into Available alerts the customer and clears the wait list.
What to do: In admin, set that product Available. Watch the phone. Open admin Notify me demand if shown.
What you should see: Phone alert that it can be ordered. Wait list count drops. Opening the alert can help add the product.

Preconditions: Customer device allowed alerts. Order is Placed.
Use case: The customer’s phone alerts them when the shop moves the order.
What to do: In admin, Confirm, then later Out for delivery.
What you should see: A phone alert for each of those steps. Opening it relates to that order.

Preconditions: Admin → Announcements → Inbox & phone. At least one customer with a push token.
Use case: The shop can send an important update to every customer inbox and phone.
What to do: Type Important update. Title under 80 characters, body under 280. Send.
What you should see: Green toast: Saved for N customers. Phone alert sent to N devices (N can be 0 if nobody allowed alerts). History shows the send.

Preconditions: Inbox & phone tab.
Use case: The shop can send an offer.
What to do: Type Offer. Title and body. Send.
What you should see: Same style of toast. Customer Offers filter shows it. Home posters do not change.

Preconditions: Ability to notice a failed phone send (or a past fail toast).
Use case: Inbox is saved even if the phone alert fails.
What to do: Send a message. If the toast says Phone alert failed, open the customer bell.
What you should see: Customer still has the message in Notifications. Bell updated. Phone may have no banner.

Preconditions: Inbox & phone tab.
Use case: Title and body have length limits.
What to do: Try a title over 80 characters or a body over 280. Try empty title.
What you should see: The form blocks send or shows an error. Nothing is sent.

Preconditions: At least one previous Inbox & phone send.
Use case: Send history stays on Inbox & phone.
What to do: Open Announcements → Inbox & phone. Scroll the history.
What you should see: Recent title, type, time, and recipient count are listed.

Preconditions: Home already has a poster.
Use case: Sending an inbox message does not change Home posters.
What to do: Send an update from Inbox & phone. Open the customer Home.
What you should see: Posters are unchanged. Only the bell/list (and phone) got the text message.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. Poster image on the computer or phone.
Use case: The shop can put a poster on the customer home screen.
What to do: Announcements → Poster. Add a poster, fit it in the wide frame. Showing on. Phone alert off. Publish.
What you should see: Customer Home shows that wide poster under the categories, not over the product list. At most 8 posters. More than one can rotate.

Preconditions: Customers who allowed notifications. Poster tab.
Use case: A phone alert goes out only for posters the shop switches on.
What to do: Turn Phone alert on for one poster, Publish. Publish again with the switch off. Also Publish while Showing is off.
What you should see: One phone alert for that poster. After publish, Phone alert is off again. Hidden announcements can still save with no alert.

Preconditions: Shop is open. Customer has a Placed order they can still modify.
Use case: The shop can stop new orders from the customer app.
What to do: Shop status → Shop is closed, write a message, Save. Customer tries Place order and Update order. Admin creates a phone order. Then Shop is open, Save.
What you should see: Home and cart show the message. Place order is not available. Update order still works. Admin can still create an order. After open, customers can place again.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. Logo file ready.
Use case: The shop saves the logo, phone, email, and address printed on the delivery bill.
What to do: Profile: logo, name, phone, email, address. Save.
What you should see: Saved successfully. Later bill uses that logo and address. Home posters stay under Announcements.

Preconditions: Admin signed in.
Use case: The shop can set a minimum order amount.
What to do: Open Preferences. Set min order (for example 200). Save. In the customer app, try Place order under and then over that amount.
What you should see: Preferences saves. Under the minimum, Place order is blocked with a clear message. At or above, it works.

Preconditions: At least one delivered unpaid order.
Use case: The shop can see who still owes money.
What to do: Open Reports. Look at Outstanding.
What you should see: Every delivered unpaid order is listed with customer, phone, amount. Total matches Dashboard outstanding.

Preconditions: Orders across more than one day.
Use case: The shop can look at sales for a chosen period.
What to do: Try Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days. Optional status or payment filter.
What you should see: Summary cards change with the period. Cancelled orders are not counted in sales.

Preconditions: Admin and/or delivery actions already happened.
Use case: The shop can see a history of important changes.
What to do: Audit log. Filter last 7 days, admin only, then delivery app only.
What you should see: Each row shows when, which app, and a short summary. Order lines open that order.

Preconditions: Driver changed an order status.
Use case: Delivery actions show up in the shop’s history.
What to do: On the website, Audit log → filter Delivery app.
What you should see: A row for that action from the delivery app.

Preconditions: Admin signed in. A customer address exists.
Use case: The shop can group addresses. Customers never see this.
What to do: Customers → Communities → turn on. Create a community. Map an address.
What you should see: Orders for that address can be filtered as that community. Customer app does not show the community name.

Preconditions: Customer signed in.
Use case: A customer saves where the order should be delivered.
What to do: Add an address: house/flat, area, 6-digit pincode, label, receiver name and phone. Save up to 3. Try a fourth.
What you should see: City and state fill from pincode. Cannot save a fourth until you delete one. The address you pick becomes default.

Preconditions: Customer signed in.
Use case: The customer can see their account, privacy, and sign out.
What to do: Tap the round initial on Home. Check name and email. Open Privacy Policy. Tap Sign out.
What you should see: Details look right. Privacy Policy includes order change/cancel, inbox (latest 20), and Notify me. After sign out you must sign in again to order.

Preconditions: App used once while online. Cart may have items.
Use case: Without internet, the customer can look but not place an order.
What to do: Turn on airplane mode. Browse. Try Place order.
What you should see: You see you are offline. Saved products can stay in the cart. Place order, sign in, and Your Orders need the internet.

Preconditions: Fresh install or cleared app data. Stay offline.
Use case: A first-time open with no internet shows a simple offline screen.
What to do: Open the app while offline.
What you should see: A full You are Offline screen with Reload.

Preconditions: Driver signed in. Orders exist for today.
Use case: The driver sees what still needs delivering today.
What to do: Look at To deliver and Delivered today.
What you should see: To deliver: Placed, Confirmed, or Out for delivery. Delivered today: delivered today (India time).

Preconditions: An order the driver can advance.
Use case: The driver moves the order forward from the phone.
What to do: Open an order. Swipe Confirm, Start delivery, Mark delivered as allowed.
What you should see: Website and customer app show the same new status. Customer inbox/phone get the matching order alerts.

Preconditions: Admin already marked Delivered.
Use case: The phone does not deliver twice.
What to do: Open the same order in the delivery app.
What you should see: App refreshes. Not asked to deliver again. Can still record payment if Not yet. Bill share is for when the driver marks delivered, not payment-only.

Preconditions: An order with phone and address.
Use case: The driver can call the customer or open maps.
What to do: On an order card, tap Call and Map.
What you should see: Dialer opens. Maps opens for the address.

Preconditions: Order just marked delivered in the delivery app.
Use case: The driver can send the bill on WhatsApp.
What to do: Tap WhatsApp. On another order try Not now. On Out for delivery or Delivered, tap Bill.
What you should see: WhatsApp can send a PDF named shop-order (for example Farm2Flavour-100111.pdf). Not now closes. Bill opens the same share sheet. The app does not send by itself.

Preconditions: A shared invoice PDF.
Use case: The bill is a one-page invoice readable from the top.
What to do: Open the PDF.
What you should see: Starts at the top. Shop logo, name, phone, email, address from Profile, Invoice, date, order number, customer, Item/Qty/Unit price/Amount, To pay, payment method, thank-you.

Preconditions: A mixed order (Kg, Liter, pack, qty).
Use case: Delivery and WhatsApp bill show the same units as the customer order.
What to do: Open the order in delivery. Share the bill.
What you should see: Items read like Coconut – 2 × 500g, Oil – 2 × 500ml, pack × 250g, qty × 3. Totals match.

Preconditions: Play Store test install (not Expo Go).
Use case: After two real new orders, Play may ask for a rating.
What to do: Place two successful new orders (not cart updates).
What you should see: Google may show a rating box once. OK if it does not. App must not crash.

App category: Order app → Admin panel → Delivery app
Preconditions: Shop open. Customer signed in with address. Preview APK. Admin HTTPS.
Use case: One real order goes from the customer all the way to paid.
What to do: 1. Customer places an order. 2. Shop confirms, sends out, delivers (website or delivery app). 3. Record Cash or UPI. Optional bill share. 4. Check customer Notifications for the three order alerts.
What you should see: Customer sees Delivered. Reports no longer shows unpaid. Inbox has confirmed / out for delivery / delivered. This is the main check before launch.
